questions.promptHtml: A team needs a central Azure resource for jobs, assets, compute, and access control used by its machine learning project. What should it create?

options.label: An Azure Machine Learning workspace
A Microsoft Foundry project resource
An Azure AI Search service

questions.correctLabel: An Azure Machine Learning workspace
questions.rationaleHtml:
A Machine Learning workspace is the top-level resource for coordinating Azure Machine Learning jobs, assets, compute, and security.

Reference: Azure Machine Learning workspace
questions.extraHtml: A workspace governs the ML lifecycle. A Foundry project organizes generative AI development, while AI Search indexes and retrieves content rather than managing ML training operations.

questions.promptHtml: Training jobs must access an existing ADLS Gen2 location without copying its files into the workspace. Which workspace object should reference it?

options.label: A versioned data asset
An Azure Machine Learning datastore
An Azure Machine Learning environment

questions.correctLabel: An Azure Machine Learning datastore
questions.rationaleHtml:
A datastore securely stores connection information that lets jobs access an external storage service.

Reference: Create and manage datastores
questions.extraHtml: A datastore represents the storage connection; a data asset identifies particular data within storage. An environment defines runtime dependencies and cannot provide storage connectivity.

questions.promptHtml: A nightly training workload needs multiple CPU nodes only while jobs run and must scale to zero afterward. Which compute target is best?

options.label: A permanently running compute instance
An attached Azure Kubernetes cluster
A managed compute cluster with minimum nodes set to zero

questions.correctLabel: A managed compute cluster with minimum nodes set to zero
questions.rationaleHtml:
A managed compute cluster can autoscale across nodes and deallocate all nodes when idle.

Reference: Create a compute cluster
questions.extraHtml: Compute instances suit interactive development and remain single-node. Attached Kubernetes is appropriate when the organization needs cluster control, but adds operational overhead for an elastic training requirement.

questions.promptHtml: A data scientist needs an individually managed cloud workstation for notebooks, terminals, and interactive debugging. Which target should be provisioned?

options.label: An Azure Machine Learning compute instance
An Azure Machine Learning compute cluster
An Azure Machine Learning batch endpoint

questions.correctLabel: An Azure Machine Learning compute instance
questions.rationaleHtml:
A compute instance is a managed development environment intended for interactive work by an individual user.

Reference: Compute instance
questions.extraHtml: A compute cluster is optimized for scalable job execution, while a batch endpoint performs asynchronous inference. Use instances for authoring and clusters for repeatable production runs.

questions.promptHtml: A pipeline must read blobs without storing account keys in code. Security requires revocable Azure authorization and least privilege. What should be configured?

options.label: A shared access signature embedded in the component YAML
The workspace managed identity with an appropriate data-plane role
The storage account key saved as a GitHub repository secret

questions.correctLabel: The workspace managed identity with an appropriate data-plane role
questions.rationaleHtml:
Managed identity plus Azure RBAC enables credential-free access and narrowly scoped authorization.

Reference: Authentication with managed identities
questions.extraHtml: SAS tokens and account keys are secrets that require rotation and can be overprivileged. Managed identity removes secret distribution while RBAC controls the exact storage scope and actions.

questions.promptHtml: A curated training folder must be referenced by a stable name, versioned when its definition changes, and mounted by jobs. Which asset type fits?

options.label: A uri_folder data asset
A custom Docker environment
A registered MLflow model

questions.correctLabel: A uri_folder data asset
questions.rationaleHtml:
A uri_folder data asset creates a versioned reference to a folder that jobs can download or mount.

Reference: Create data assets
questions.extraHtml: Data assets describe inputs and preserve lineage without necessarily duplicating data. Environments package dependencies; models package inference artifacts rather than source training folders.

questions.promptHtml: Training must use the same Python and CUDA dependencies in development and CI runs. Which reusable asset should the team version?

options.label: A compute instance schedule
An Azure Machine Learning environment
A workspace diagnostic setting

questions.correctLabel: An Azure Machine Learning environment
questions.rationaleHtml:
An environment versions the Docker image and Python dependencies used to execute jobs consistently.

Reference: Manage environments
questions.extraHtml: Compute schedules control availability and diagnostic settings route logs. Environments address runtime reproducibility and should be pinned to explicit versions in production jobs.

questions.promptHtml: A preprocessing step will be reused in several pipelines and must declare inputs, outputs, code, and runtime independently. What should be created?

options.label: A reusable command component
A standalone online deployment
A storage lifecycle policy

questions.correctLabel: A reusable command component
questions.rationaleHtml:
A component packages executable logic with its interface and environment for reuse in pipelines.

Reference: Azure Machine Learning components
questions.extraHtml: Components are modular pipeline building blocks that support versioning and lineage. Online deployments serve requests, and lifecycle policies manage stored objects rather than ML workflow logic.

questions.promptHtml: Two workspaces in different subscriptions must consume the same approved models, components, and environments. Which service should hold these assets?

options.label: A shared Azure Machine Learning registry
A shared Log Analytics workspace
A shared Azure Container Registry repository only

questions.correctLabel: A shared Azure Machine Learning registry
questions.rationaleHtml:
A registry shares versioned Machine Learning assets across workspaces and organizational boundaries.

Reference: Manage Azure Machine Learning registries
questions.extraHtml: A container registry shares images but not complete ML asset metadata, lineage, models, and components. Log Analytics centralizes telemetry rather than reusable ML assets.

questions.promptHtml: A GitHub Actions workflow must submit Azure ML jobs without a long-lived client secret. Which authentication pattern should be used?

options.label: A storage account access key in GitHub secrets
OpenID Connect federation with an Azure identity
A workspace user token committed to the repository

questions.correctLabel: OpenID Connect federation with an Azure identity
questions.rationaleHtml:
GitHub OIDC federation exchanges a short-lived token for Azure access and avoids stored client credentials.

Reference: Connect GitHub Actions to Azure with OpenID Connect
questions.extraHtml: OIDC reduces secret rotation and leakage risk. Storage keys do not authenticate Azure Resource Manager operations, and user tokens are unsuitable for unattended automation.

questions.promptHtml: Development and production workspaces must be recreated consistently through pull requests. Which approach provides declarative and repeatable resource deployment?

options.label: Manual creation in Azure portal with screenshots
An Azure CLI script containing interactive prompts
Version-controlled Bicep modules with parameter files

questions.correctLabel: Version-controlled Bicep modules with parameter files
questions.rationaleHtml:
Bicep provides declarative Azure infrastructure definitions that can be reviewed, parameterized, and repeatedly deployed.

Reference: Bicep overview
questions.extraHtml: Portal steps are difficult to audit and reproduce. CLI can be automated, but interactive imperative scripts provide weaker desired-state semantics than parameterized Bicep modules.

questions.promptHtml: Infrastructure changes must be validated on pull requests and deployed only after merge to the main branch. What should orchestrate this policy?

options.label: A recurring Azure Machine Learning pipeline schedule
Separate GitHub Actions workflows triggered by pull_request and push
A notebook that an administrator runs after each merge

questions.correctLabel: Separate GitHub Actions workflows triggered by pull_request and push
questions.rationaleHtml:
GitHub Actions event triggers can validate proposed IaC on pull requests and deploy approved changes after a push to the protected branch.

Reference: Use GitHub Actions with Azure Machine Learning
questions.extraHtml: ML pipeline schedules orchestrate model workflows, not repository governance. Manual notebooks weaken auditability; protected branches plus event-driven workflows separate validation from deployment.

questions.promptHtml: An Azure ML workspace must be reachable only from approved virtual networks while public access is disabled. Which configuration meets the requirement?

options.label: A private endpoint with private DNS integration
A public endpoint protected only by resource locks
A service health alert scoped to the workspace

questions.correctLabel: A private endpoint with private DNS integration
questions.rationaleHtml:
Private Link exposes the workspace through a private IP, while private DNS resolves workspace endpoints inside the virtual network.

Reference: Configure a private endpoint
questions.extraHtml: Resource locks prevent deletion or modification but do not filter network traffic. Health alerts report platform issues and provide no network isolation.

questions.promptHtml: A team needs reviewable history for training code, component YAML, and environment definitions while large datasets remain in cloud storage. What should be placed in Git?

options.label: Source and declarative definitions, excluding data and generated artifacts
Every training dataset and model binary in normal Git objects
Only notebook outputs, excluding scripts and configuration files

questions.correctLabel: Source and declarative definitions, excluding data and generated artifacts
questions.rationaleHtml:
Git should track code and configuration; durable data and large model artifacts belong in managed data and model stores.

Reference: Git integration for Azure Machine Learning
questions.extraHtml: Committing large data bloats repository history and risks data exposure. Notebook outputs are generated state; the reproducible inputs—code and definitions—are the important reviewable assets.

questions.promptHtml: A datastore accesses ADLS Gen2 through the identity of each interactive user, so storage permissions must differ by user. Which datastore authentication mode is appropriate?

options.label: Account-key authentication shared by every user
Identity-based authentication with user credentials
Anonymous public-container authentication

questions.correctLabel: Identity-based authentication with user credentials
questions.rationaleHtml:
Identity-based access can pass through the signed-in user's identity so storage RBAC determines individual authorization.

Reference: Data authentication administration
questions.extraHtml: A shared key erases per-user accountability and grants common privileges. Anonymous access cannot enforce identity-specific permissions and is inappropriate for protected training data.

questions.promptHtml: A CPU cluster is idle most weekends but receives unpredictable weekday jobs. How should it minimize cost without delaying cluster recreation?

options.label: Delete and redeploy the cluster after every job
Keep one node running continuously for readiness
Set minimum nodes to zero and configure an idle timeout

questions.correctLabel: Set minimum nodes to zero and configure an idle timeout
questions.rationaleHtml:
Autoscaling to zero releases compute cost after the configured idle period while preserving the cluster definition.

Reference: Configure compute cluster autoscaling
questions.extraHtml: Deleting infrastructure adds provisioning overhead and operational churn. A permanent node reduces startup latency but violates the cost-minimization requirement during long idle periods.

questions.promptHtml: A production job unexpectedly changes behavior after a curated environment receives a new version. Which practice best preserves reproducibility?

options.label: Reference the environment by name and explicit version
Resolve the newest environment version at each run
Rebuild dependencies from unpinned package names

questions.correctLabel: Reference the environment by name and explicit version
questions.rationaleHtml:
Pinning the environment asset version gives each job a stable and auditable runtime definition.

Reference: Manage environment versions
questions.extraHtml: Using latest introduces silent runtime changes. Unpinned package resolution is even less deterministic because upstream packages can change without an Azure ML asset update.

questions.promptHtml: A pipeline step is unchanged, but teams repeatedly copy its YAML and code into new projects. Which action best improves governance and reuse?

options.label: Convert the step into a versioned component
Convert the step into an online endpoint
Convert the step into a datastore credential

questions.correctLabel: Convert the step into a versioned component
questions.rationaleHtml:
A versioned component exposes a stable contract and can be reused without duplicating implementation details.

Reference: Machine Learning component concepts
questions.extraHtml: Endpoints host inference and datastores provide storage connections. Neither supplies the composable interface, lineage, and runtime encapsulation needed for pipeline reuse.

questions.promptHtml: A central platform team publishes an approved model, and regional workspaces must consume that exact version without separate copies owned by each team. What should they reference?

options.label: A model asset in a Machine Learning registry
A model file attached to a GitHub release
A model output inside one workspace job

questions.correctLabel: A model asset in a Machine Learning registry
questions.rationaleHtml:
Registry assets are centrally versioned and can be referenced from jobs or deployments in multiple workspaces.

Reference: Manage models in registries
questions.extraHtml: GitHub releases lack Azure ML deployment metadata and governance. A job output is scoped operational state until it is registered and is not a governed cross-workspace contract.

questions.promptHtml: A training script logs parameters, metrics, and artifacts, and analysts need a standard experiment UI without custom tracking infrastructure. What should be integrated?

options.label: MLflow tracking in Azure Machine Learning
Azure Policy compliance scan results
Azure Storage lifecycle management

questions.correctLabel: MLflow tracking in Azure Machine Learning
questions.rationaleHtml:
Azure ML integrates with MLflow to record runs, parameters, metrics, and artifacts in workspace experiments.

Reference: MLflow and Azure Machine Learning
questions.extraHtml: Policy evaluates resource compliance, and storage lifecycle rules move or delete blobs. Neither provides experiment semantics or comparison of model-training runs.

questions.promptHtml: A supported scikit-learn training script needs automatic capture of common parameters, metrics, and model artifacts with minimal logging code. Which MLflow capability should be enabled?

options.label: Model serving with a batch endpoint
MLflow autologging for the framework
Data drift monitoring on the input asset

questions.correctLabel: MLflow autologging for the framework
questions.rationaleHtml:
MLflow autologging automatically records framework-specific training information and artifacts.

Reference: Log and view metrics with MLflow
questions.extraHtml: Serving and drift monitoring happen after or outside training. Autologging reduces instrumentation effort, though explicit logging remains useful for custom business metrics.

questions.promptHtml: A team wants Azure to test preprocessing and algorithm combinations for a labeled tabular classification dataset under a time budget. Which capability is appropriate?

options.label: Automated machine learning classification
A manual sweep over one script parameter
A responsible AI dashboard for one model

questions.correctLabel: Automated machine learning classification
questions.rationaleHtml:
Automated ML explores supported algorithms and featurization choices while honoring experiment constraints.

Reference: Automated machine learning
questions.extraHtml: A sweep tunes parameters defined by the author but does not broadly select algorithms and preprocessing. A responsible AI dashboard analyzes an existing model rather than searching candidates.

questions.promptHtml: A data scientist is exploring distributions and debugging feature code interactively before converting the work into a repeatable job. Which tool is most suitable now?

options.label: A managed online endpoint deployment
A notebook on a compute instance
A scheduled batch endpoint invocation

questions.correctLabel: A notebook on a compute instance
questions.rationaleHtml:
Notebooks provide interactive code execution and visualization for exploration on managed development compute.

Reference: Run Jupyter notebooks
questions.extraHtml: Endpoints are production inference interfaces and do not provide an exploratory authoring loop. Once exploration stabilizes, move logic into scripts and components for reproducibility.

questions.promptHtml: A training job must evaluate learning rate and batch size combinations in parallel and select the run with the best validation score. What should be submitted?

options.label: A hyperparameter sweep job
A model monitor definition
A managed feature store materialization job

questions.correctLabel: A hyperparameter sweep job
questions.rationaleHtml:
A sweep job samples a defined parameter space and optimizes child runs against a primary metric.

Reference: Tune hyperparameters
questions.extraHtml: Model monitoring evaluates production behavior, while feature materialization computes feature values. Neither launches comparative training trials against an optimization metric.

questions.promptHtml: Many weak hyperparameter trials consume the full budget even after their metric is clearly worse than leading runs. Which change reduces wasted compute?

options.label: Increase the maximum nodes of the cluster
Configure an early termination policy
Disable the primary optimization metric

questions.correctLabel: Configure an early termination policy
questions.rationaleHtml:
An early termination policy stops poorly performing child runs according to intermediate metric results.

Reference: Early termination of sweep runs
questions.extraHtml: More nodes increase concurrency but not efficiency per trial. The primary metric is required to compare runs; early termination conserves budget without eliminating optimization guidance.

questions.promptHtml: Production training must execute a Python script noninteractively with declared inputs, outputs, environment, and compute. Which Azure ML job type is the direct fit?

options.label: A command job
An interactive notebook session
An online inference request

questions.correctLabel: A command job
questions.rationaleHtml:
A command job runs a specified command on managed compute with explicit data and environment dependencies.

Reference: Train models with jobs
questions.extraHtml: Notebooks are suited to exploration and can hide state. Online requests invoke deployed inference; they do not provide repeatable training execution and output lineage.

questions.promptHtml: A deep learning job no longer fits efficiently on one GPU and must coordinate training across several GPU nodes. What should the job configure?

options.label: A parallel distribution strategy such as PyTorch or MPI
A larger batch endpoint retry count
A semantic ranker configuration for the dataset

questions.correctLabel: A parallel distribution strategy such as PyTorch or MPI
questions.rationaleHtml:
Azure ML distribution settings launch and coordinate processes across GPUs and nodes for supported frameworks.

Reference: Distributed training
questions.extraHtml: Endpoint retries concern inference reliability, and semantic ranking concerns search relevance. Distributed training also requires code and framework behavior compatible with multi-process execution.

questions.promptHtml: Data preparation, training, and evaluation must execute as a dependency graph with reusable steps and recorded lineage. What should the team build?

options.label: A sequence of portal operations documented in a wiki
An Azure Machine Learning pipeline job
A single long-running online deployment

questions.correctLabel: An Azure Machine Learning pipeline job
questions.rationaleHtml:
A pipeline composes components into a directed workflow with dependencies, inputs, outputs, and lineage.

Reference: Machine Learning pipelines
questions.extraHtml: Manual portal actions are not repeatable, and online deployments serve predictions rather than orchestrating training stages. Components keep pipeline steps independently reusable.

questions.promptHtml: A pipeline reruns daily, but an expensive preprocessing component should reuse prior output whenever its code, environment, and inputs are unchanged. Which feature helps?

options.label: Component output reuse in the pipeline
Online endpoint traffic mirroring
Workspace soft-delete protection

questions.correctLabel: Component output reuse in the pipeline
questions.rationaleHtml:
Azure ML can reuse a prior component result when the step definition and relevant inputs remain unchanged.

Reference: Pipeline reuse
questions.extraHtml: Traffic mirroring validates deployments, and soft delete protects resources. Neither avoids repeated deterministic pipeline computation; disable reuse only for genuinely nondeterministic steps.

questions.promptHtml: Twenty training runs used different parameters. The team needs to sort them by validation AUC and inspect metrics side by side. Which mechanism should it use?

options.label: Experiment run comparison using logged MLflow metrics
Storage account metrics grouped by container
Endpoint access logs grouped by status code

questions.correctLabel: Experiment run comparison using logged MLflow metrics
questions.rationaleHtml:
Logged runs can be queried and compared by metrics and parameters to identify candidate models.

Reference: Track experiments with MLflow
questions.extraHtml: Storage and endpoint telemetry describe infrastructure and serving behavior, not validation quality across training candidates. Consistent metric names are essential for reliable comparisons.

questions.promptHtml: An online model requires point-in-time feature retrieval at inference, and its retrieval definition must travel with the model artifact. What should registration include?

options.label: A packaged feature retrieval specification
A compute cluster autoscale schedule
A workspace private DNS zone export

questions.correctLabel: A packaged feature retrieval specification
questions.rationaleHtml:
Packaging the retrieval specification with the model preserves the feature contract needed for consistent serving.

Reference: Managed feature store concepts
questions.extraHtml: Autoscale and DNS settings govern infrastructure, not feature semantics. Coupling the retrieval specification to the model reduces training-serving skew and improves deployment reproducibility.

questions.promptHtml: A model logged during training must become a governed, versioned workspace asset that can be deployed later. Which action is required?

options.label: Register the MLflow model in Azure Machine Learning
Leave the artifact only in the temporary run output
Copy the pickle file into the source repository

questions.correctLabel: Register the MLflow model in Azure Machine Learning
questions.rationaleHtml:
Registration creates a named and versioned model asset from the MLflow artifact.

Reference: Manage MLflow models
questions.extraHtml: Run outputs provide lineage but are not the promoted deployment contract. Git is unsuitable for large binaries and lacks Azure ML model lifecycle metadata.

questions.promptHtml: A retrained model uses the same logical name but must coexist with the currently deployed model until validation finishes. How should it be registered?

options.label: Overwrite the deployed model files in place
Create a new version under the same model name
Rename the workspace before every retraining run

questions.correctLabel: Create a new version under the same model name
questions.rationaleHtml:
Model versions preserve immutable candidates under a stable logical name for comparison and controlled promotion.

Reference: Register and manage model versions
questions.extraHtml: In-place mutation destroys provenance and rollback safety. Workspace renaming does not version an artifact and disrupts dependent automation.

questions.promptHtml: Before promoting a loan model, reviewers must inspect performance disparities across demographic cohorts and understand influential features. Which capability should they use?

options.label: Responsible AI dashboard analysis
Compute cluster node diagnostics
Azure Resource Graph inventory

questions.correctLabel: Responsible AI dashboard analysis
questions.rationaleHtml:
The Responsible AI dashboard combines model explanations, error analysis, and fairness-oriented cohort assessment.

Reference: Responsible AI dashboard
questions.extraHtml: Compute diagnostics investigate infrastructure, while Resource Graph inventories Azure resources. Responsible evaluation complements—not replaces—domain review and governance decisions.

questions.promptHtml: An obsolete model must no longer appear in normal active-model workflows, but audit history and lineage must be retained. What should be done?

options.label: Delete every run and artifact permanently
Archive the registered model asset
Move the workspace to another subscription

questions.correctLabel: Archive the registered model asset
questions.rationaleHtml:
Archiving removes an asset from active use while preserving its metadata and history for governance.

Reference: Manage the model lifecycle
questions.extraHtml: Permanent deletion conflicts with retention and audit requirements. Subscription movement changes resource ownership but does not express lifecycle status for the model.

questions.promptHtml: A fraud-scoring API must return one prediction synchronously for each request with low latency. Which deployment target is appropriate?

options.label: A managed online endpoint
A recurring batch endpoint job
A training pipeline schedule

questions.correctLabel: A managed online endpoint
questions.rationaleHtml:
Online endpoints provide synchronous request-response inference for low-latency applications.

Reference: Online endpoints
questions.extraHtml: Batch endpoints process large asynchronous datasets and do not serve interactive calls. Pipeline schedules orchestrate workflows rather than expose inference APIs.

questions.promptHtml: A retailer scores 50 million records overnight and writes results to storage; no caller waits for an immediate response. Which target should it use?

options.label: A managed online endpoint with one request per row
An Azure Machine Learning batch endpoint
A compute instance running an open notebook

questions.correctLabel: An Azure Machine Learning batch endpoint
questions.rationaleHtml:
Batch endpoints provide asynchronous, scalable inference over large datasets and persist outputs.

Reference: Batch endpoints
questions.extraHtml: Online endpoints add per-request overhead for an offline workload. An interactive notebook lacks production scheduling, isolation, retry, and scalable parallel execution.

questions.promptHtml: A team wants Azure to provision and patch the inference infrastructure while it controls deployment instances and scaling. Which option minimizes operational burden?

options.label: A managed online endpoint
A self-managed Kubernetes web service
A virtual machine with a custom API daemon

questions.correctLabel: A managed online endpoint
questions.rationaleHtml:
Managed online endpoints handle serving infrastructure while exposing deployment, instance, traffic, and scaling controls.

Reference: Managed online endpoints
questions.extraHtml: Kubernetes and VMs offer more infrastructure control but require cluster or host operations. Choose them only when requirements justify that additional responsibility.

questions.promptHtml: A new online deployment returns HTTP 500 responses. The team needs container startup output and scoring-script exceptions. What should it inspect first?

options.label: Deployment logs for the managed online endpoint
The model card description in the registry
Git branch protection audit events

questions.correctLabel: Deployment logs for the managed online endpoint
questions.rationaleHtml:
Deployment logs expose container initialization and scoring failures needed to diagnose unhealthy inference replicas.

Reference: Troubleshoot online endpoints
questions.extraHtml: Model descriptions and Git governance do not show runtime exceptions. Also validate locally and invoke the endpoint with representative payloads before shifting production traffic.

questions.promptHtml: A replacement model must receive 10% of production requests while the current model receives 90%, with both behind one endpoint URL. What should be configured?

options.label: Weighted traffic allocation across two deployments
Two unrelated workspaces with separate DNS names
A batch deployment with ten parallel workers

questions.correctLabel: Weighted traffic allocation across two deployments
questions.rationaleHtml:
An online endpoint can split traffic by percentage among deployments to support controlled rollout.

Reference: Safely roll out online endpoints
questions.extraHtml: Separate endpoints complicate client routing and measurement. Batch worker count controls parallel offline processing, not request allocation between model versions.

questions.promptHtml: A team wants to observe how a candidate deployment responds to live requests without returning its predictions to callers. Which rollout technique should it use?

options.label: Mirrored traffic to the candidate deployment
Fifty-percent weighted production traffic
A permanent batch scoring schedule

questions.correctLabel: Mirrored traffic to the candidate deployment
questions.rationaleHtml:
Traffic mirroring sends copies of requests to a deployment while excluding its responses from client results.

Reference: Mirror online endpoint traffic
questions.extraHtml: Weighted traffic exposes users to candidate responses, which violates the constraint. Batch scoring cannot reproduce live request shape, timing, or serving conditions.

questions.promptHtml: Error rate rises immediately after all endpoint traffic moves to the new deployment. The old deployment is still healthy. What is the fastest safe response?

options.label: Retrain the new model while it serves all traffic
Reallocate traffic to the previous deployment
Delete the endpoint and create a different workspace

questions.correctLabel: Reallocate traffic to the previous deployment
questions.rationaleHtml:
Keeping the prior deployment available enables rapid rollback by changing endpoint traffic weights.

Reference: Rollback an online deployment
questions.extraHtml: Retraining does not immediately protect users, and endpoint deletion creates unnecessary downtime. Define health thresholds and automated rollback criteria before rollout.

questions.promptHtml: A model's input distributions may change after deployment even though ground-truth labels arrive weeks later. Which signal can detect this earliest?

options.label: Data drift between baseline and production inputs
Workspace resource-group naming drift
Git commit frequency for training scripts

questions.correctLabel: Data drift between baseline and production inputs
questions.rationaleHtml:
Data drift monitoring compares production feature distributions with a reference dataset without requiring immediate labels.

Reference: Model monitoring
questions.extraHtml: Infrastructure naming and source activity do not measure statistical changes in model inputs. Drift signals risk; it does not by itself prove that predictive quality declined.

questions.promptHtml: Labels for production predictions are available. Which measure most directly reveals whether a classifier's quality has degraded?

options.label: Prediction performance metrics computed against ground truth
Average CPU utilization of inference replicas
Number of registered environment versions

questions.correctLabel: Prediction performance metrics computed against ground truth
questions.rationaleHtml:
Comparing predictions with ground truth enables direct monitoring of quality metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, or AUC.

Reference: Monitor model performance
questions.extraHtml: CPU utilization indicates infrastructure load, not correctness. Asset counts are governance metadata; neither can establish predictive degradation.

questions.promptHtml: A production model should be checked every day against a recent data window without manual execution. What should the team configure?

options.label: A scheduled model monitoring job
An always-open notebook kernel
A repository issue template

questions.correctLabel: A scheduled model monitoring job
questions.rationaleHtml:
A scheduled monitor repeatedly computes configured signals over production data and baseline windows.

Reference: Configure model monitoring
questions.extraHtml: Notebook kernels are interactive and fragile for operations, while issue templates only standardize human reports. Monitoring schedules should align with data arrival and business response time.

questions.promptHtml: Retraining is costly and must start only after a drift metric exceeds the approved limit, while operators must also be notified. Which design is best?

options.label: Trigger an alert and an automated retraining workflow from the threshold breach
Retrain continuously after every individual prediction
Wait for an annual manual review regardless of the metric

questions.correctLabel: Trigger an alert and an automated retraining workflow from the threshold breach
questions.rationaleHtml:
Threshold-driven automation links monitored degradation to timely notification and controlled retraining.

Reference: Production model monitoring
questions.extraHtml: Per-prediction retraining is wasteful and unstable, while annual review ignores the required response. Promotion should still require evaluation gates rather than automatically replacing production.

questions.promptHtml: A batch deployment processes many independent files too slowly on one node. The scoring code already supports mini-batches. Which change improves throughput?

options.label: Increase batch parallelism and instance count
Convert the workload into one synchronous request
Disable partitioning of the input dataset

questions.correctLabel: Increase batch parallelism and instance count
questions.rationaleHtml:
Batch deployments can divide input into mini-batches and process them concurrently across compute instances.

Reference: Use batch model deployments
questions.extraHtml: One synchronous request sacrifices batch scalability and risks timeout. Disabling partitioning prevents parallel work distribution and worsens the bottleneck.

questions.promptHtml: Only approved callers should invoke a managed online endpoint, and keys must not be distributed. Which authentication mode best fits?

options.label: Microsoft Entra token authentication
Anonymous public access
A shared endpoint key in source control

questions.correctLabel: Microsoft Entra token authentication
questions.rationaleHtml:
Microsoft Entra authentication supports identity-based access and avoids distributing static endpoint keys.

Reference: Authenticate clients for online endpoints
questions.extraHtml: Anonymous access cannot enforce caller identity, and committed keys are easily leaked and shared. Pair identity authentication with least-privilege role assignments.

questions.promptHtml: A batch endpoint invocation failed on several mini-batches because input files were malformed. Where should operators look for per-job failure details?

options.label: The batch job logs and output/error artifacts
The workspace's model description field
The repository's pull request labels

questions.correctLabel: The batch job logs and output/error artifacts
questions.rationaleHtml:
Each batch invocation creates a job whose logs and artifacts expose scoring and mini-batch failures.

Reference: Troubleshoot batch endpoints
questions.extraHtml: Model metadata and PR labels cannot reveal runtime parsing errors. A robust scoring script should log failed items and define retry/error-threshold behavior deliberately.

questions.promptHtml: A team must promote only models whose test metric exceeds 0.90 and whose responsible AI review is approved. Where should this decision be enforced?

options.label: In an automated deployment gate before production traffic changes
In the endpoint description after deployment completes
In a compute instance startup script for each developer

questions.correctLabel: In an automated deployment gate before production traffic changes
questions.rationaleHtml:
A release gate can evaluate model metrics and governance approvals before a candidate is promoted.

Reference: Machine learning operations process
questions.extraHtml: Descriptions document state but do not enforce it, and developer startup scripts are not centralized release controls. Keep evaluation evidence immutable and tied to the registered model version.

questions.promptHtml: The same pipeline definition must run with different datasets in development and production without editing component code. What design supports this?

options.label: Parameterize pipeline inputs and environment-specific bindings
Hard-code production storage paths in every component
Duplicate the entire pipeline for each dataset version

questions.correctLabel: Parameterize pipeline inputs and environment-specific bindings
questions.rationaleHtml:
Explicit pipeline inputs separate reusable workflow logic from environment-specific data references.

Reference: Create component pipelines
questions.extraHtml: Hard-coding reduces portability and may expose production paths. Duplication causes configuration drift; parameterization preserves one governed workflow definition.

questions.promptHtml: A model candidate has better aggregate accuracy but performs substantially worse for a protected cohort. What should block automatic promotion?

options.label: A responsible AI acceptance criterion for cohort performance
A lower compute-cluster idle timeout
A newer Docker base image tag

questions.correctLabel: A responsible AI acceptance criterion for cohort performance
questions.rationaleHtml:
Promotion criteria should include disaggregated performance and fairness risks, not only aggregate quality.

Reference: Responsible AI assessment
questions.extraHtml: Compute cost and image freshness matter operationally but do not resolve harmful cohort disparity. Human governance should define acceptable tradeoffs and escalation paths.

questions.promptHtml: A Foundry team needs a governed boundary for connections, deployments, agents, evaluations, and collaborators for one application. What should it create?

options.label: A Microsoft Foundry project
An Azure Machine Learning datastore
An Azure Monitor action group

questions.correctLabel: A Microsoft Foundry project
questions.rationaleHtml:
A Foundry project organizes application resources, connections, deployments, assets, and team access.

Reference: What is Microsoft Foundry
questions.extraHtml: A datastore abstracts storage connectivity, while an action group routes alerts. Neither provides the application development and governance boundary required here.

questions.promptHtml: A Foundry application must access Azure AI Search without API keys. Which configuration is preferred?

options.label: A managed identity assigned an appropriate Search data role
An admin key embedded in the system prompt
A query key committed to the application repository

questions.correctLabel: A managed identity assigned an appropriate Search data role
questions.rationaleHtml:
Managed identity and Azure RBAC provide credential-free, least-privilege access to the search service.

Reference: Use managed identities in Foundry
questions.extraHtml: Admin keys grant broad privileges and prompts can leak. Query keys are less privileged but remain static secrets requiring distribution and rotation.

questions.promptHtml: A developer should build and evaluate a Foundry application but must not change project role assignments. Which access design follows least privilege?

options.label: Assign the narrow project-level development role needed
Assign Owner at the subscription scope
Share the project administrator's access token

questions.correctLabel: Assign the narrow project-level development role needed
questions.rationaleHtml:
Azure RBAC should grant only required actions at the smallest practical scope.

Reference: Role-based access control in Foundry
questions.extraHtml: Subscription Owner can modify access across unrelated resources, and token sharing destroys identity and audit boundaries. Separate resource administration from application development duties.

questions.promptHtml: A regulated Foundry deployment must keep service traffic on private IP addresses and disable public network access. What should be implemented?

options.label: Private endpoints and correctly linked private DNS zones
Public endpoints protected only by randomized names
Resource locks on every project and deployment

questions.correctLabel: Private endpoints and correctly linked private DNS zones
questions.rationaleHtml:
Private Link and DNS integration route supported service access privately from approved networks.

Reference: Configure private networking for Foundry
questions.extraHtml: Obscure names are not a security boundary, and resource locks prevent changes rather than network access. Validate every dependency because private networking must cover the complete data path.

questions.promptHtml: Development, test, and production Foundry environments must use identical topology but different names and capacities. Which deployment method is best?

options.label: Parameterized Bicep templates invoked by automation
Repeated manual portal configuration in each environment
Exported screenshots stored with the application source

questions.correctLabel: Parameterized Bicep templates invoked by automation
questions.rationaleHtml:
Parameterized IaC keeps topology consistent while allowing controlled environment-specific values.

Reference: Create Foundry resources with templates
questions.extraHtml: Manual recreation encourages drift, and screenshots are documentation rather than executable desired state. Validate changes with what-if before deployment.

questions.promptHtml: A team wants to call a catalog model through a provider-managed API and avoid managing virtual machines or containers. Which deployment type should it choose?

options.label: A serverless API deployment
A self-hosted Kubernetes deployment
A local compute instance deployment

questions.correctLabel: A serverless API deployment
questions.rationaleHtml:
Serverless API deployments expose supported catalog models as managed endpoints without customer-managed serving infrastructure.

Reference: Deploy models as serverless APIs
questions.extraHtml: Kubernetes is appropriate for custom infrastructure control but adds operations. A compute instance is an interactive development machine, not a production serving service.

questions.promptHtml: A specialized model requires a custom inference environment and dedicated compute sizing not offered by its serverless option. Which deployment approach fits?

options.label: Managed compute deployment in Foundry
A prompt asset with no model deployment
A Log Analytics saved query

questions.correctLabel: Managed compute deployment in Foundry
questions.rationaleHtml:
Managed compute supports model serving with selected compute and deployment configuration when serverless APIs do not meet requirements.

Reference: Deploy models to managed compute
questions.extraHtml: Prompts orchestrate model behavior but do not host model weights. Saved queries analyze telemetry and cannot execute inference.

questions.promptHtml: A customer-support application prioritizes instruction following, supported context length, regional availability, and cost. How should the team choose a foundation model?

options.label: Evaluate eligible catalog models against representative tasks and constraints
Select the model with the largest parameter count automatically
Select whichever model was added to the catalog most recently

questions.correctLabel: Evaluate eligible catalog models against representative tasks and constraints
questions.rationaleHtml:
Model selection should combine workload requirements, availability, safety, quality evaluation, latency, and cost.

Reference: Models in Microsoft Foundry
questions.extraHtml: Parameter count and release date are weak proxies and may conflict with cost, region, context, or latency requirements. Representative evaluation provides workload-specific evidence.

questions.promptHtml: A provider announces a new model version, but production must remain reproducible until regression tests pass. What should the deployment reference?

options.label: An explicitly selected model version
An automatically resolved latest alias only
An unversioned model name stored in a notebook cell

questions.correctLabel: An explicitly selected model version
questions.rationaleHtml:
Pinning a model version prevents unreviewed provider updates from silently changing production behavior.

Reference: Model versions and upgrades
questions.extraHtml: Latest-style resolution trades control for convenience. Use a staged deployment and evaluation suite before deliberately promoting a newer model version.

questions.promptHtml: A new foundation-model deployment must be tested with a small share of users and rolled back quickly if quality falls. Which strategy is appropriate?

options.label: A canary rollout with measured promotion gates
Immediate replacement of the only production deployment
Manual prompt edits directly in the production portal

questions.correctLabel: A canary rollout with measured promotion gates
questions.rationaleHtml:
A canary strategy limits exposure, compares production signals, and retains a known-good rollback target.

Reference: Safe deployment practices
questions.extraHtml: Immediate replacement increases blast radius. Unversioned portal edits bypass review and make attribution or rollback difficult.

questions.promptHtml: A high-volume generative AI workload needs predictable reserved capacity and stable latency rather than consumption-based shared throughput. What should be configured?

options.label: Provisioned throughput units
A larger Log Analytics retention period
A higher Azure AI Search replica count only

questions.correctLabel: Provisioned throughput units
questions.rationaleHtml:
Provisioned throughput reserves model-processing capacity for predictable high-volume workloads.

Reference: Provisioned throughput
questions.extraHtml: Telemetry retention does not affect inference capacity, and search replicas improve retrieval throughput rather than language-model token processing.

questions.promptHtml: Traffic is intermittent and low, and the application can tolerate variable shared-service latency. Which capacity model generally avoids paying for reserved model throughput?

options.label: Standard consumption-based deployment
Provisioned throughput deployment
Dedicated GPU virtual machines kept online

questions.correctLabel: Standard consumption-based deployment
questions.rationaleHtml:
Standard deployments charge for usage and are often appropriate for variable workloads that do not justify reserved capacity.

Reference: Azure OpenAI deployment types
questions.extraHtml: Provisioned throughput targets predictable sustained demand, while dedicated VMs add management and idle cost. Validate regional availability and quota before choosing a type.

questions.promptHtml: A planned PTU deployment fails despite valid Bicep syntax because the subscription cannot allocate the requested model capacity in that region. What should be checked?

options.label: Model quota and capacity availability for the region
The Git repository's default branch name
The prompt's groundedness evaluation score

questions.correctLabel: Model quota and capacity availability for the region
questions.rationaleHtml:
Model deployments depend on subscription quota and available capacity for the chosen model, version, type, and region.

Reference: Azure OpenAI quota and limits
questions.extraHtml: Branch naming and prompt quality cannot resolve resource allocation failure. Capacity planning should precede production-region selection and IaC rollout.

questions.promptHtml: A prompt change must be reviewed, reproduced, and correlated with evaluation results. How should the prompt be managed?

options.label: Store the prompt as a version-controlled source artifact
Edit only the live deployment with no saved history
Save the prompt in a developer's terminal history

questions.correctLabel: Store the prompt as a version-controlled source artifact
questions.rationaleHtml:
Git-based prompt management provides history, review, branching, and linkage to tests and releases.

Reference: Develop and manage generative AI flows
questions.extraHtml: Direct production edits and shell history lack governed review and reproducibility. Treat prompts, model settings, tools, and evaluation data as coordinated release inputs.

questions.promptHtml: Two system prompts differ in tone and instruction ordering. The team needs objective evidence about which performs better. What should it do?

options.label: Evaluate both variants on the same representative dataset and metrics
Compare only the character count of each prompt
Deploy the newer prompt to all users without a baseline

questions.correctLabel: Evaluate both variants on the same representative dataset and metrics
questions.rationaleHtml:
Controlled evaluation isolates prompt variation while holding test examples and scoring criteria constant.

Reference: Evaluate generative AI applications
questions.extraHtml: Prompt length is a cost signal, not a quality verdict. Full deployment without baseline evidence increases risk and prevents a controlled comparison.

questions.promptHtml: Developers frequently overwrite one another's prompt changes and cannot reproduce the version used in last week's release. Which practice fixes both issues?

options.label: Branch, review, and tag prompt files in Git
Share one mutable prompt in a team chat message
Put the latest prompt only in an endpoint description

questions.correctLabel: Branch, review, and tag prompt files in Git
questions.rationaleHtml:
Git workflows preserve immutable history and enable collaborative review and release tagging.

Reference: What is version control
questions.extraHtml: Chat and descriptions are mutable communication surfaces, not source-control systems. Release tags should identify prompt, configuration, and model versions together.

questions.promptHtml: A production agent calls Azure services on behalf of the application. Credentials must rotate automatically and each call must be attributable to the workload. What should it use?

options.label: The project's managed identity with scoped RBAC
A developer's personal access token
A subscription key pasted into agent instructions

questions.correctLabel: The project's managed identity with scoped RBAC
questions.rationaleHtml:
A managed workload identity supplies short-lived tokens and auditable authorization without embedded secrets.

Reference: Managed identity for Foundry projects
questions.extraHtml: Personal tokens couple production to a person, and prompts are unsafe secret stores. Scope each tool's permissions independently where practical.

questions.promptHtml: A Foundry project needs governed access to an existing Azure AI Search service used by its RAG application. Which project object should represent that dependency?

options.label: A configured project connection
A model evaluation dataset
A prompt variant label

questions.correctLabel: A configured project connection
questions.rationaleHtml:
Project connections define how Foundry applications access dependent Azure and external resources.

Reference: Add connections to a Foundry project
questions.extraHtml: Evaluation datasets measure behavior, and variant labels distinguish prompt alternatives. Neither establishes resource connectivity or authentication.

questions.promptHtml: An automation identity needs to create model deployments but must not grant roles to other principals. Which control should enforce this?

options.label: A custom or built-in RBAC role excluding role-assignment actions
Subscription Owner assigned to the automation identity
Shared use of a Global Administrator account

questions.correctLabel: A custom or built-in RBAC role excluding role-assignment actions
questions.rationaleHtml:
Least-privilege RBAC can permit resource deployment while withholding Microsoft.Authorization role-assignment permissions.

Reference: Azure role-based access control
questions.extraHtml: Owner includes access delegation, and shared administrative accounts defeat separation of duties. Scope the role to the resource group or project where possible.

questions.promptHtml: A pull request changes a model SKU and network setting in Bicep. The team wants to preview Azure resource changes before approval. Which operation should CI run?

options.label: An Azure Resource Manager what-if deployment
A production model inference benchmark only
A destructive resource-group deletion test

questions.correctLabel: An Azure Resource Manager what-if deployment
questions.rationaleHtml:
What-if predicts resource additions, removals, and modifications without applying the Bicep deployment.

Reference: Bicep what-if operation
questions.extraHtml: Inference benchmarks test runtime performance but not infrastructure drift. Destructive tests are unnecessary and unsafe for change preview.

questions.promptHtml: Clients must keep a stable logical endpoint while a tested model version replaces the old one. Which practice best decouples clients from model versions?

options.label: Route through a stable deployment or application endpoint name
Embed the provider's model version in every client binary
Require users to discover a new URL after each release

questions.correctLabel: Route through a stable deployment or application endpoint name
questions.rationaleHtml:
A stable abstraction lets operators change the backing model through a controlled release without coordinating every client.

Reference: Create and deploy Azure OpenAI models
questions.extraHtml: Hard-coded versions and changing URLs tightly couple clients to releases. Preserve version details in deployment metadata and observability for auditability.

questions.promptHtml: A model's default safety behavior is insufficient for an application's policy, but the team still needs platform-level filtering at inference. What should be associated with the deployment?

options.label: A configured content filter policy
A higher embedding vector dimension
A compute cluster idle shutdown rule

questions.correctLabel: A configured content filter policy
questions.rationaleHtml:
Content filtering can be configured and applied to model deployments to enforce supported harm-category thresholds.

Reference: Configure content filters
questions.extraHtml: Embedding dimensions affect retrieval representation, and compute shutdown affects cost. Filtering is one defense layer and does not replace application safeguards or evaluation.

questions.promptHtml: A team needs to compare model offerings, deployment options, task capabilities, and benchmarks before selecting a foundation model. Where should it start?

options.label: The Foundry model catalog
The Azure Policy compliance dashboard
The Machine Learning datastore list

questions.correctLabel: The Foundry model catalog
questions.rationaleHtml:
The model catalog supports discovery and comparison of available foundation models and deployment paths.

Reference: Explore the model catalog
questions.extraHtml: Policy reports governance compliance and datastores list storage connections. Neither supplies model capability and deployment metadata.

questions.promptHtml: A deployment pipeline must create a Foundry resource, project, and dependent services in a deterministic order. Which design is most maintainable?

options.label: Modular Bicep with explicit resource dependencies and outputs
Independent portal clicks performed in any order
One notebook cell containing undocumented REST calls

questions.correctLabel: Modular Bicep with explicit resource dependencies and outputs
questions.rationaleHtml:
Bicep modules and dependency expressions make provisioning order and resource contracts reviewable and repeatable.

Reference: Bicep modules
questions.extraHtml: Portal operations are manual, and undocumented notebook calls obscure idempotency and failure handling. Module outputs should pass resource identifiers rather than duplicate naming logic.

questions.promptHtml: A model performs well in English but the production workload includes Spanish and Japanese. What should happen before model selection is finalized?

options.label: Evaluate candidate models on representative multilingual examples
Assume benchmark leadership guarantees equal language quality
Translate all outputs after deployment without testing inputs

questions.correctLabel: Evaluate candidate models on representative multilingual examples
questions.rationaleHtml:
Workload-specific evaluation must represent languages, tasks, and distributions expected in production.

Reference: Evaluate models and applications
questions.extraHtml: Aggregate benchmarks can hide language-specific weaknesses. Post-translation adds another model and does not validate understanding of multilingual inputs.

questions.promptHtml: A project has separate development and production model deployments. Operators need to know exactly which prompt commit and model version formed each release. What should be recorded?

options.label: Immutable release metadata linking prompt commit and deployment version
Only the current prompt text in a shared document
Only the model family name in the resource group tag

questions.correctLabel: Immutable release metadata linking prompt commit and deployment version
questions.rationaleHtml:
Release traceability requires a durable mapping among source, prompt, configuration, model, and deployment versions.

Reference: GenAIOps for generative AI
questions.extraHtml: A mutable document loses history, while a model family omits prompt and configuration changes. Complete linkage enables rollback and root-cause analysis.

questions.promptHtml: A customer-facing assistant will be evaluated before release. The team needs examples covering normal requests, edge cases, and known failures with expected context fields. What should it create?

options.label: A representative versioned test dataset
A larger production compute instance
A private DNS zone for evaluation results

questions.correctLabel: A representative versioned test dataset
questions.rationaleHtml:
A curated test dataset supplies stable inputs and context for repeatable application and model evaluation.

Reference: Prepare data for evaluation
questions.extraHtml: Compute size affects execution speed and DNS controls name resolution. Neither defines what quality and risk cases are tested.

questions.promptHtml: An evaluator expects fields named query, response, and context, but the test file uses question, answer, and passages. What must be configured?

options.label: Data mapping from dataset columns to evaluator inputs
A new provisioned throughput deployment
A content filter with higher severity thresholds

questions.correctLabel: Data mapping from dataset columns to evaluator inputs
questions.rationaleHtml:
Evaluation data mapping binds application dataset fields to the evaluator's required input schema.

Reference: Evaluation data mapping
questions.extraHtml: Throughput and filtering affect serving and safety, not evaluator schema compatibility. Incorrect mapping can produce invalid or misleading scores.

questions.promptHtml: A RAG assistant gives a fluent answer that contains claims absent from the retrieved documents. Which quality metric most directly exposes the problem?

options.label: Groundedness
Fluency
Throughput

questions.correctLabel: Groundedness
questions.rationaleHtml:
Groundedness measures whether response claims are supported by the supplied context.

Reference: Built-in evaluation metrics
questions.extraHtml: Fluency measures linguistic quality and can be high for fabricated claims. Throughput measures operational capacity, not factual support from retrieved evidence.

questions.promptHtml: An answer is fully supported by documents but does not address the user's actual question. Which metric should be emphasized?

options.label: Relevance
Groundedness
Token consumption

questions.correctLabel: Relevance
questions.rationaleHtml:
Relevance assesses how well the response addresses the user's query and informational need.

Reference: Quality evaluation metrics
questions.extraHtml: Groundedness can be high for an off-topic but supported statement. Token consumption measures cost and size rather than task alignment.

questions.promptHtml: A generated report contradicts itself between sections even though each sentence is grammatical. Which metric targets this weakness?

options.label: Coherence
Fluency
Request latency

questions.correctLabel: Coherence
questions.rationaleHtml:
Coherence evaluates logical consistency, organization, and meaningful flow across the response.

Reference: Coherence evaluation
questions.extraHtml: Fluency focuses on language form and readability; latency measures speed. A response can be fluent and fast while logically inconsistent.

questions.promptHtml: A response contains awkward grammar and unnatural phrasing but follows a logically consistent outline. Which metric best captures the defect?

options.label: Fluency
Coherence
Groundedness

questions.correctLabel: Fluency
questions.rationaleHtml:
Fluency measures grammatical correctness, readability, and natural language quality.

Reference: Fluency evaluation
questions.extraHtml: Coherence evaluates logical structure, while groundedness checks support from context. These quality dimensions should be evaluated separately to avoid masking tradeoffs.

questions.promptHtml: Before launch, an agent must be tested for hateful, sexual, violent, and self-harm content across adversarial prompts. What evaluation should be run?

options.label: Risk and safety evaluation
Retrieval latency benchmark only
Embedding dimensionality analysis

questions.correctLabel: Risk and safety evaluation
questions.rationaleHtml:
Risk and safety evaluators assess supported harmful-content categories and severities in generated interactions.

Reference: Risk and safety evaluators
questions.extraHtml: Latency and vector dimensions do not measure harmful output. Combine pre-release red-team-style cases, platform controls, and post-release monitoring.

questions.promptHtml: A legal assistant has a domain rule that citations must use an approved identifier format. No built-in metric checks it. What should the team add?

options.label: A custom evaluator for citation compliance
A larger standard model deployment
A lower search similarity threshold

questions.correctLabel: A custom evaluator for citation compliance
questions.rationaleHtml:
Custom evaluators encode application-specific quality rules not covered by general built-in metrics.

Reference: Create custom evaluators
questions.extraHtml: A larger model may still violate formatting, and search thresholds affect retrieval candidates. Explicit domain metrics make release criteria measurable.

questions.promptHtml: Every pull request that changes a prompt must run the same evaluation suite and fail when quality drops below thresholds. Where should this run?

options.label: An automated CI workflow
An annual manual production review
An interactive notebook with no saved results

questions.correctLabel: An automated CI workflow
questions.rationaleHtml:
CI evaluation provides consistent regression checks before prompt changes merge or deploy.

Reference: Continuous evaluation for generative AI
questions.extraHtml: Annual review is too late, and unsaved notebook runs are not enforceable or auditable. Version the dataset and evaluator configuration with the release inputs.

questions.promptHtml: Offline tests pass, but production traffic evolves over time. Which capability should detect ongoing quality changes on sampled live interactions?

options.label: Continuous monitoring in Foundry
A one-time local unit test run
A resource-group naming convention

questions.correctLabel: Continuous monitoring in Foundry
questions.rationaleHtml:
Continuous monitoring evaluates operational traces and quality signals after deployment to detect changes in real usage.

Reference: Monitor generative AI applications
questions.extraHtml: Unit tests remain useful but cannot observe distribution shifts in live traffic. Naming conventions aid organization, not behavioral detection.

questions.promptHtml: Users report that responses feel slow. Which metric most directly quantifies time from request submission until the response completes?

options.label: End-to-end response latency
Tokens per billing month
Groundedness score

questions.correctLabel: End-to-end response latency
questions.rationaleHtml:
End-to-end latency captures user-perceived request duration across retrieval, orchestration, model inference, and post-processing.

Reference: Monitor application performance
questions.extraHtml: Monthly tokens quantify usage and groundedness measures context support. Trace spans are then needed to identify which stage dominates latency.

questions.promptHtml: A service meets single-request latency targets but cannot sustain the required requests per minute during peak load. Which metric reveals this limitation?

options.label: Throughput
Coherence
Citation precision

questions.correctLabel: Throughput
questions.rationaleHtml:
Throughput measures the amount of work completed per unit time and exposes capacity constraints under load.

Reference: Latency and throughput
questions.extraHtml: Coherence and citation precision are quality measures. Diagnose throughput alongside rate limits, concurrency, token sizes, and deployment capacity.

questions.promptHtml: A generative AI application's monthly cost rises although request count is stable. Which telemetry should be examined first?

options.label: Input and output token consumption by operation
Number of Git branches in the prompt repository
Count of private DNS records in the virtual network

questions.correctLabel: Input and output token consumption by operation
questions.rationaleHtml:
Token telemetry reveals whether larger prompts, retrieved context, or responses increased model usage per request.

Reference: Monitor cost and token usage
questions.extraHtml: Source branches and DNS records do not drive model token billing. Correlate tokens with model deployment, route, customer, and prompt version to locate regressions.

questions.promptHtml: An agent intermittently calls the wrong tool. Operators need to reconstruct model calls, tool calls, timing, and errors for one request. What should be enabled?

options.label: Distributed tracing with correlated spans and detailed logs
Only aggregate monthly token totals
Only Azure Resource Manager activity logs

questions.correctLabel: Distributed tracing with correlated spans and detailed logs
questions.rationaleHtml:
Traces show the sequence and timing of application, model, retrieval, and tool operations for a request.

Reference: Trace generative AI applications
questions.extraHtml: Aggregate totals lack request detail, while activity logs record management-plane changes rather than agent execution. Redact sensitive prompt and tool data according to policy.

questions.promptHtml: A release dashboard shows average latency is acceptable, but a small group experiences severe delays. Which analysis should be added?

options.label: Tail latency percentiles such as p95 and p99
Only the arithmetic mean latency
Only the total number of model deployments

questions.correctLabel: Tail latency percentiles such as p95 and p99
questions.rationaleHtml:
High percentiles reveal slow outliers hidden by an acceptable average and better represent poor user experiences.

Reference: Performance testing guidance
questions.extraHtml: The mean can conceal a long tail, and deployment counts say nothing about request duration. Segment percentiles by model, route, region, and prompt version.

questions.promptHtml: RAG retrieval returns many weakly related passages that distract the model. Relevant documents usually score much higher. What should be tuned first?

options.label: Raise the similarity threshold using evaluation evidence
Increase response temperature for more variety
Increase model output-token allowance

questions.correctLabel: Raise the similarity threshold using evaluation evidence
questions.rationaleHtml:
A higher similarity cutoff can exclude low-relevance retrieval results when score separation supports that choice.

Reference: Vector query configuration
questions.extraHtml: Temperature and output limits affect generation, not which passages are retrieved. Tune thresholds against recall and relevance because an excessive cutoff can omit needed evidence.

questions.promptHtml: Large documents are indexed as entire files, causing broad embeddings and oversized context. Which change is most likely to improve retrieval precision?

options.label: Split documents into semantically meaningful chunks with controlled overlap
Concatenate all documents into one index record
Remove document metadata before indexing

questions.correctLabel: Split documents into semantically meaningful chunks with controlled overlap
questions.rationaleHtml:
Chunking creates focused retrieval units while overlap can preserve concepts crossing boundaries.

Reference: Chunk documents for vector search
questions.extraHtml: A single record reduces granularity, and removing metadata discards useful filtering and citation context. Evaluate chunk size rather than assuming smaller is always better.

questions.promptHtml: A RAG system retrieves one excellent passage but often misses a second passage needed to answer multi-part questions. Which parameter should be evaluated?

options.label: The number of top results returned
The model's maximum output tokens only
The deployment's content filter severity only

questions.correctLabel: The number of top results returned
questions.rationaleHtml:
Increasing top-k can improve retrieval recall for questions requiring evidence from multiple chunks.

Reference: Configure vector query results
questions.extraHtml: Generation limits and content filters do not add retrieved evidence. Larger top-k can add noise and cost, so tune it with end-to-end relevance evaluation.

questions.promptHtml: A multilingual legal corpus uses specialized terminology. The current general embedding model performs poorly on cross-language retrieval. What is the best next step?

options.label: Evaluate multilingual or domain-suitable embedding models on labeled query-document pairs
Select an embedding model solely by its vector dimension
Increase the chat model temperature during retrieval

questions.correctLabel: Evaluate multilingual or domain-suitable embedding models on labeled query-document pairs
questions.rationaleHtml:
Embedding selection should be based on retrieval quality for representative languages and domain semantics.

Reference: Select models in Foundry
questions.extraHtml: Dimension affects storage and compatibility but does not prove relevance. Chat temperature applies during generation and cannot repair the embedding space.

questions.promptHtml: An embedding model is adapted for a medical vocabulary. What must happen before it replaces the production embedding model?

options.label: Re-embed indexed content and validate queries in a compatible index
Keep old document vectors and change only query embeddings
Change the chat model without touching the search index

questions.correctLabel: Re-embed indexed content and validate queries in a compatible index
questions.rationaleHtml:
Queries and documents must be encoded into the same compatible embedding space for meaningful vector similarity.

Reference: Create a vector index
questions.extraHtml: Mixing old document vectors with new query embeddings yields invalid similarity comparisons. Use a parallel index for safe evaluation and rollback.

questions.promptHtml: Users search with exact product codes plus natural-language descriptions. Which retrieval design best combines lexical precision and semantic similarity?

options.label: Hybrid search with keyword and vector queries
Vector search with all text fields removed
Keyword search with embeddings disabled permanently

questions.correctLabel: Hybrid search with keyword and vector queries
questions.rationaleHtml:
Hybrid search executes lexical and vector retrieval together and merges their results.

Reference: Hybrid search overview
questions.extraHtml: Vector-only retrieval can miss exact identifiers, while keyword-only retrieval can miss paraphrases. Hybrid retrieval is especially useful when both behaviors matter.

questions.promptHtml: Hybrid retrieval returns a strong candidate set, but ranking still poorly reflects the meaning of complex natural-language questions. Which feature can rerank the results?

options.label: Semantic ranker
Storage lifecycle management
Compute instance autostop

questions.correctLabel: Semantic ranker
questions.rationaleHtml:
Semantic ranker applies language understanding to rerank an initial search result set for semantic relevance.

Reference: Semantic ranking in Azure AI Search
questions.extraHtml: Storage lifecycle and compute schedules control cost, not search ordering. Semantic ranking complements retrieval and does not replace a well-designed index or filters.

questions.promptHtml: A team changes chunk size and retrieval strategy. Which evaluation most directly determines whether the retriever improved before generation?

options.label: Retrieval relevance metrics on labeled query-document judgments
GPU utilization of the chat model deployment
Grammatical fluency of generated answers only

questions.correctLabel: Retrieval relevance metrics on labeled query-document judgments
questions.rationaleHtml:
Retriever metrics compare returned documents with relevance judgments and isolate search quality from generation behavior.

Reference: Retrieval evaluation metrics
questions.extraHtml: GPU utilization is operational, and answer fluency can remain high with poor evidence. Also run end-to-end groundedness and relevance tests before release.

questions.promptHtml: Two RAG configurations pass offline tests. The team needs evidence from real users while limiting risk. Which experiment is appropriate?

options.label: A randomized A/B test with predefined success and guardrail metrics
A full replacement with no control group
A comparison of configuration file lengths

questions.correctLabel: A randomized A/B test with predefined success and guardrail metrics
questions.rationaleHtml:
A controlled A/B test estimates causal performance differences while monitoring quality, safety, latency, and cost.

Reference: GenAIOps experimentation
questions.extraHtml: Full replacement confounds change with time and raises blast radius. File length has no reliable relationship to user outcomes.

questions.promptHtml: A base model follows general instructions but repeatedly mishandles a stable, specialized output task despite prompt optimization and sufficient examples. Which customization may help?

options.label: Supervised fine-tuning with curated input-output examples
Increasing search replicas without using retrieval
Adding more private DNS records to the project

questions.correctLabel: Supervised fine-tuning with curated input-output examples
questions.rationaleHtml:
Supervised fine-tuning can adapt model behavior to a recurring task using high-quality labeled demonstrations.

Reference: Fine-tuning considerations
questions.extraHtml: Search capacity and DNS do not teach model behavior. Fine-tuning should follow prompt and RAG baselines because it adds data, evaluation, cost, and lifecycle obligations.

questions.promptHtml: A fine-tuning project lacks enough examples of rare but important cases. The team plans to generate synthetic examples. Which practice is essential?

options.label: Validate synthetic data for correctness, diversity, and leakage before training
Accept every generated example without review
Replace the real validation set with synthetic training data

questions.correctLabel: Validate synthetic data for correctness, diversity, and leakage before training
questions.rationaleHtml:
Synthetic data can expand coverage but requires quality controls to avoid amplifying errors, bias, duplication, or contamination.

Reference: Synthetic data generation
questions.extraHtml: Unreviewed examples can teach false patterns. Keep an independent representative validation set so evaluation does not merely reward synthetic artifacts.

questions.promptHtml: A fine-tuned model improves task accuracy but doubles latency and increases harmful-output failures. What should determine promotion?

options.label: A multi-metric gate covering quality, safety, latency, and cost
Task accuracy alone regardless of regressions
The number of completed training epochs alone

questions.correctLabel: A multi-metric gate covering quality, safety, latency, and cost
questions.rationaleHtml:
Production readiness is a constrained optimization problem; improvement in one metric cannot excuse failed operational or safety requirements.

Reference: Deploy and evaluate fine-tuned models
questions.extraHtml: Accuracy and epoch count are insufficient decision criteria. Define thresholds before training and compare against the base-model baseline on identical tests.

questions.promptHtml: A new fine-tuned model version is approved, but production rollback must remain immediate. Which release approach is best?

options.label: Register and deploy it as a separate version, then shift traffic gradually
Overwrite the only production model artifact in place
Delete the prior deployment before testing the new model

questions.correctLabel: Register and deploy it as a separate version, then shift traffic gradually
questions.rationaleHtml:
Separate immutable versions support controlled promotion, comparison, traceability, and rapid rollback.

Reference: Deploy a fine-tuned model
questions.extraHtml: In-place overwrite and early deletion remove the known-good rollback target. Keep training data, hyperparameters, base model, evaluations, and deployment metadata linked to each version.
